Breunig shared on Hacker News the prompts he used with Opus 5.5 to build the system, starting by having it read Agrawal's original article and source code before exploring how to emulate the chip and RAM inside Qwen. stories.title: Claude agent autonomously chose and delivered gene therapy to a mouse
stories.summary: A Claude-based AI agent autonomously chose a gene therapy drug, target, and injection coordinates, then performed brain surgery on an epileptic mouse — reportedly the first time an agent has chosen and delivered a treatment to a living mammal unaided.
stories.more: Lead researcher Ocana-Santero says this is the first time an AI agent has autonomously selected a treatment and delivered it to a living mammal without human decision-making. The Claude-based agent picked the drug, the brain target, and the injection coordinates for a gene therapy procedure on an epileptic mouse, then performed the surgery itself. When a calibration error occurred mid-surgery, the agent refused to continue and could not be talked out of stopping. The excerpt doesn't specify the gene therapy's target condition's outcome or next steps for the research.

stories.title: Youtu-Parsing-Omni paper unifies parsing across text, image, audio, video
stories.summary: Researchers introduce Youtu-Parsing-Omni, an omni-modal parser that converts documents, images, audio, and video into structured, space-time-grounded records using one shared encoder and one schema, aiming to give AI agents a unified way to read, locate, and cite evidence across modalities.
stories.more: The system is designed as a perception layer for AI agents that need to read, locate, and cite evidence across different media types. It relies on a single encoder architecture and a single schema applied across all modalities and tasks, rather than separate pipelines per modality. That encoder, called Youtu-Omni-Encoder, is initialized from a pretrained language model to strengthen its text-reading ability. It then encodes documents, images, audio, and video with shared weights inside a unified space-time coordinate system. The paper does not detail benchmark results in the available excerpt.

stories.title: Study proves JEPAs converge to the same representation across modalities
stories.summary: A new paper turns the Platonic Representation Hypothesis into a proven theorem, showing that Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPAs) trained separately on different modalities converge to the same representation up to a single rotation.
stories.more: The Platonic Representation Hypothesis holds that models trained on different modalities converge toward the same underlying representation of the world as they scale, but until now it had no formal proof. This paper supplies one, proving what it calls a Platonic Representation Theorem. It shows that Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures, or JEPAs, trained separately on any number of modalities learn representations that match up to a single rotation. The excerpt does not specify which modalities or datasets were tested, or how the theorem translates into practical guidance for training such models.

stories.title: SpecSlot decouples image detail from token count in pixel Transformers
stories.summary: A new paper introduces SpecSlot, a pixel-space rectified-flow Transformer that separates fine image detail from the number of tokens used, letting low-frequency structure use global attention while high-frequency detail is modeled locally.
stories.more: Pixel-space generative Transformers normally assign one token per image patch, so adding finer detail means adding more tokens and making global attention more expensive. The authors argue this isn't necessary: low-frequency structure benefits from global information exchange, but high-frequency detail can be captured with local modeling instead. Based on that observation, they introduce SpecSlot, a pixel-space rectified-flow Transformer that decouples output detail from token length. The excerpt is cut off before describing how the architecture achieves this split or what results it reports.
